payload.name: Enumerate places visited in a specific time window
payload.description: When a question asks which places (or all places) a person visited during a specific month or period, gather every candidate location memory, verify timestamps, and expand searches with discovered place and activity terms before answering.
content: When a question asks which places a person visited in a specific time window, treat it as an enumeration task: keep searching until follow-up queries stop surfacing new candidate place memories, and do not answer from the first retrieved location alone.

For each retrieved travel/activity memory, extract its named places and activity descriptors (e.g., road trip, skiing, hiking) and use those as additional query terms in later searches instead of reusing the original query or the first place name.

Before counting a candidate place, verify its memory world_start/world_end falls within the requested period; exclude any candidate whose timestamp is outside the window even if it is the only or highest-scoring result.
When multiple candidates have in-period evidence, include all distinct places in the answer rather than selecting a single one.

solves: Future questions that ask which places (including 'which places...', 'all places...') a person visited during a specific month or period. The diagnosed cause is that the agent anchored on the first retrieved location, used an out-of-window memory as evidence, and missed other in-window places because follow-up searches reused the original query rather than terms mined from retrieved memories. The rule transfers to any location enumeration question with a temporal constraint; it does not apply to open-ended location questions without a time window.
